name: ARTEMIS
one_liner: Turns written instructions into automation on real Android phones.

text.why: Android app tests wire a script to every screen element, and it breaks as soon as the screen changes. ARTEMIS takes instructions in plain language and drives a real device or emulator itself; over MCP, Antigravity, Claude Code and Windsurf can call the phone and collect Logcat output and screenshots. One start script installs ADB, scrcpy and FFmpeg and opens a browser console (Apache-2.0). The first task installs a small accessibility helper on the phone.
text.take: Hand it a sentence instead of a test script, and get back what a real phone actually did.
build: A pre-release regression run of login and checkout on a real device
A QA report that reproduces a bug and attaches logs and screenshots
A nightly long-running exploration test for app stability

who.situation: scripts keep breaking as screens change
wants device logs and screenshots inside the IDE
needs a pre-release check without a QA team

start.text: Connect an Android device with USB debugging on, or an emulator, first
Windows PowerShell: .\start.bat · opens localhost:8000 in the browser

caveat: The first task installs an accessibility helper on the phone (removable)
iOS is on the roadmap, not supported yet
Python 3.12+ and uv; the start script auto-installs system tools
